DAN is a robust face alignment algorithm that can handle face images with a large variation in head poses and difficult initializations, and that DAN reduces the failure rate of the state-of-the art face alignment methods by up to 60%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following contributions: • We introduce a new deep network architecture for robust face alignment.
the problem of face alignment, i.e. finding the locations of the 68 facial landmarks on an input face image.

the following contributions: (1) we propose DAN which is the first deep learning based method for face alignment; (2) we propose landmark heatmaps which are used in our method to allow the use of entire face image for face alignment; and (3) we show that DAN is robust to difficult initializations and large variations in head pose.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is robust to large variations in head pose and outperforms all other methods.
DAN is a very promising approach to robust face alignment.
the proposed method has been able to outperform all the existing methods on all the datasets and metrics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to achieve a 70% reduction in failure rate compared to the state-of-the art.
we propose an end-to-end deep neural network architecture which can be trained to learn robust facial landmark detectors for face alignment.
our approach achieves state-of-the-art results on both the Menpo Challenge dataset and the publicly available 300-W dataset.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the robustness of a face alignment method can be improved significantly by using entire face images rather then relying on local patches.

a robust facial landmark detector can be built by using an iterative process that gradually improves the accuracy of the facial landmark locations, where each stage of the algorithm uses the entire face image rather than local patches.
a deep convolutional neural network architecture can be successfully employed to achieve robust face alignment, even in the case where the training set contains only a small number of images.
